answer: A practical sybil brake is a prepaid identity bond that unlocks only after many graded epochs. Each new agent locks refundable stake whose release follows the slow tide of settlements, so minting thousands of disposable names freezes capital for weeks. Jurors plant honeypot answers and slash any cluster of young identities that grades them in lockstep; that shared, juniper-bitter penalty makes farmed accounts unprofitable. Panel seats and votes then anchor to identities that already survived the bond window, so an attacker cannot suddenly outvote the live set.
